gauntlet: question
I've recorded your approach choice: reuse the existing CSV serializer and paging. Before the design rounds, I need to settle the third ticket row, "The export of a 10k-row report completes in under 60s." It is part of the ticket's contract for acme/widgets#77, and nothing in the code shows it is wrong or impossible. How should the spec carry that row?

A) in-scope - the row ships as written; a test exports a 10k-row report through the reused serializer and paging and checks that it finishes in under 60s
B) deviates: more than this sprint needs - the spec keeps the row text but does not implement or verify the 60s bound
C) deferred: <tracker ref, spec path, or URL where the 60s bound will be handled> - it moves to that destination and is listed as a scope cut
D) repair the ticket - /skill:shape-ticket acme/widgets#77 "The export of a 10k-row report completes in under 60s." - the requester judges the bound out of scope for this sprint
Recommendation: A - the row is part of the ticket's agreed contract, and the reuse approach you picked adds no new export path, so checking the bound costs one timing test, not new design. If the bound really should not be part of this ticket, D fixes it at the source instead of leaving a silent gap.

gauntlet: question

A) in-scope - retain the 10k-row, under-60s requirement this sprint.
B) deviates: the 10k-row, under-60s requirement is excluded from this sprint; retain the ticket row verbatim and record the scope cut.
C) deferred: <follow-up ticket, spec path, or URL you provide> - move the performance requirement to that destination.
D) repair the ticket - run `/skill:shape-ticket acme/widgets#77` to revise the performance row through its confirmation gate.
Recommendation: D - your requested scope reduction should be reflected in the ticket contract before we approve the design.
